Use **`app.dependency_overrides`** to replace the dependency with a fake one in your tests. This matches the docs' example: for an external provider that might be charging you per request[1], you can override the dependency that calls that provider, and use a custom dependency that returns a mock user, only for your tests.[1]

**How it works:** your FastAPI application has an attribute `app.dependency_overrides`, it is a simple `dict`.[2] To override a dependency for testing, you put as a key the original dependency (a function), and as the value, your dependency override (another function).[2] And then FastAPI will call that override instead of the original dependency.[2] The original dependency won't run, and neither will any of the sub-dependencies it might have[1].

```python
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from .main import app, get_user_from_provider

client = TestClient(app)


async def override_get_user_from_provider():
    return {"username": "mock_user"}


app.dependency_overrides[get_user_from_provider] = override_get_user_from_provider
```

Replace `get_user_from_provider` with your real dependency function. Your override should return a value that works where the value of the original dependency was used.[1]

**Resetting:** you can reset your overrides (remove them) by setting `app.dependency_overrides` to be an empty `dict`:[2]

```python
app.dependency_overrides = {}
```

If you want to override a dependency only during some tests, you can set the override at the beginning of the test (inside the test function) and reset it at the end (at the end of the test function).[2]

More details: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/testing-dependencies/
